h1: Samutprakarn Hotel, Pak Nam — a brand-new apartment-style stay just two minutes from the BTS
intro: If you want a freshly opened base in Mueang Pak Nam with spotless rooms and the BTS practically at your doorstep, Samutprakarn Hotel & Serviced Apartment is the name guests keep mentioning right now. This 117-room property on Sukhumvit Road in Pak Nam opened in 2025. Guests most often praise its brand-new, spotless rooms, a location just ~130m from BTS Pak Nam (Exit 3), and apartment-style rooms with a kitchenette and balcony, plus a ground-floor café, a gym and free parking. Rates start at around ฿730/night and it scores a high 9.4 from real guest reviews. Just know that some rooms feel a touch cramped from the amount of furniture, and there are a few small details a brand-new hotel is still ironing out.

body.html: What wins guests over at Samutprakarn Hotel is its newness. The property only opened in 2025, so the rooms and common areas still feel pristine, and a lot of reviews describe the rooms as spotless and barely lived in. The rooms are apartment-style, with a kitchenette, fridge, work desk and balcony, which suits anyone who wants to heat up their own food or stay several nights more than a plain hotel room would.

Location is the real selling point here. The hotel sits on Sukhumvit Road in Pak Nam, just about 130m from BTS Pak Nam station (Green Line), Exit 3 — a walk of roughly two minutes. From Pak Nam you can ride the BTS straight into central Bangkok's business districts with no transfers. Downstairs there is a 24-hour convenience store and local restaurants right across the street, so a late dinner is never far away.

"Rooms feel brand new and spotless, just a few steps to BTS Pak Nam, with a convenience store and restaurants across the road. The little café downstairs is lovely and the staff are friendly — great value for a new hotel."

On the facilities side there is a ground-floor café (guests get a discount), a gym, a garden and terrace, a 24-hour front desk, free parking and luggage storage. That works whether you arrive by car or rely on the BTS. One thing to note: this leans toward being a serviced apartment, so there is no swimming pool — if a pool is a must, look elsewhere.

Staff are another point reviews mention positively, describing them as friendly and helpful. The overall feel is calm, as Mueang Pak Nam mixes residential blocks with local shops. Sitting right on the BTS also makes it handy for travellers connecting through Suvarnabhumi Airport, since the drive from Pak Nam to the airport is short.

What to keep in mind are the usual new-hotel details still being fine-tuned. Some reviews say rooms are packed with furniture and feel a bit tight, the Deluxe King is really two single beds pushed together, the main light switch sits awkwardly behind the pillow, and the Wi-Fi runs on 5GHz only, which some older devices cannot pick up. A few guests also noted occasional cleanliness slips such as hair in the bathroom or a cup that was not properly washed, plus front-desk complaint handling that could be smoother. If any of this worries you, flag it right away at check-in and it tends to get sorted quickly.

Overall, Samutprakarn Hotel earns a high 9.4 out of 10 from more than 640 real reviews. It is a strong-value pick among Mueang Pak Nam stays — new, clean rooms, a two-minute walk to BTS Pak Nam, an in-room kitchenette and free parking. Rates start around ฿730 and climb with the season and room type (the one- and two-bedroom suites are larger and pricier). If you can live with the small quirks of a brand-new hotel and the lack of a pool, this is a convenient, good-value base in Pak Nam.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Samutprakarn Hotel, Pak Nam

faq.q: How close is Samutprakarn Hotel to BTS Pak Nam?
faq.a: Very close. The hotel is on Sukhumvit Road in Pak Nam, just about 130m from BTS Pak Nam station (Green Line), Exit 3 — roughly a 2-minute walk. From Pak Nam you can ride the BTS straight into central Bangkok's business districts with no transfers, making it ideal for travellers who rely on public transport.

faq.q: What are the rooms like and how much do they cost?
faq.a: Rooms are serviced-apartment style, with a kitchenette, fridge, work desk and balcony. They start with the Studio Twin at ~30 sqm from about ฿730/night, rising with the season and room type to around ฿1,400 for the One Bedroom Suite (~52 sqm). Always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Samutprakarn Hotel have a pool and parking?
faq.a: There is free parking, but no swimming pool, as it's a serviced apartment. The main facilities are a ground-floor café (with a guest discount), a gym, a garden and terrace, a 24-hour front desk and luggage storage. If a pool is a must, choose a resort-style stay instead.

faq.q: Who is Samutprakarn Hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits anyone wanting a new, clean room right by BTS Pak Nam to reach Bangkok, longer-stay guests who want an in-room kitchenette, and travellers connecting through Suvarnabhumi Airport. You get apartment-style rooms, a café, a gym and free parking. But with no pool and as a brand-new hotel, it's best for those prioritising convenience and value over a resort atmosphere.

faq.q: What's around Samutprakarn Hotel to eat and see?
faq.a: There's a 24-hour convenience store and local restaurants right across the road, with Pak Nam Market about a 5-minute walk away. Phra Samut Chedi, the Ancient City and the Erawan Museum are roughly 10–15 minutes by car, while Bangkok's main sights are an easy BTS ride into town.

faq.q: Are there any downsides to keep in mind?
faq.a: A few, as you'd expect from a new hotel. Some reviews note that certain rooms are packed with furniture and feel tight, the Deluxe King is two single beds pushed together, the main light switch sits behind the pillow, and the Wi-Fi is 5GHz only. A few guests also mention occasional cleanliness slips. Flag anything at check-in and it tends to get fixed quickly.
